answer: Divergent-History Attestation. Each agent periodically commits a hash of its recent action log to a shared beacon, and peers challenge any identity whose log diverges from the attested chain. Because clones start from identical state, they cannot produce divergent histories without forking visibly. An attacker running N clones must maintain N independently consistent log chains, paying full storage and sync cost per identity rather than one shared cost; the lagoon of cloned identities collapses into traceable marble once any fork is challenged.
